questions.stem: Mahatma GANDHI was BORN at Porbandar (Gujarat) in:
questions.explanation: Mohandas Karamchand GANDHI — born 2 October 1869 at PORBANDAR, GUJARAT (a princely state in Kathiawar; coastal town). Father Karamchand = diwan (PM) of Porbandar; mother Putlibai = devout Vaishnav Hindu (heavy influence on Gandhi's vegetarianism, fasting, simple living). Married KASTURBA at 13 (child marriage common then). Studied LAW in LONDON (Inner Temple, 1888-91) — in his autobiography, Gandhi confesses early struggles to fit in (clothes, food). After law degree, returned to India 1891; tried law practice (unsuccessful in Bombay + Rajkot). 1893: went to SOUTH AFRICA on a 1-year contract for Indian merchant Dada Abdulla — turned into 21 years there, transformed him into 'Mahatma'. Birthday = INTERNATIONAL DAY OF NON-VIOLENCE (UN, 2007).

questions.stem: Gandhi spent ~21 years in SOUTH AFRICA, where he developed the technique of:
questions.explanation: SATYAGRAHA — Sanskrit 'satya' (truth) + 'agraha' (insistence / firmness) = 'truth-force' / 'soul-force'. Coined by Gandhi (1906, after a competition; suggested by his cousin) to describe his non-violent civil disobedience. Roots: Tolstoy (Christian non-resistance), Thoreau (Civil Disobedience), Gita (selfless action), Jainism (ahimsa). FIRST SATYAGRAHA: 1906, JOHANNESBURG, against COMPULSORY REGISTRATION of Indians (Black Act). Famous TRAIN INCIDENT — June 1893, Pietermaritzburg: Gandhi thrown out of FIRST-CLASS coach despite valid ticket — defining moment of his political awakening. Later led: protests against £3 tax on Indians, the Indian Relief Act 1914 (Gandhi-Smuts agreement). Returned to INDIA Jan 1915 (Bombay reception). PHOENIX (1904) + TOLSTOY FARM (1910) — his ashrams in S Africa.

questions.stem: Gandhi RETURNED to India from South Africa in:
questions.explanation: Gandhi RETURNED to India 9 JAN 1915 (now celebrated as PRAVASI BHARATIYA DIVAS — NRI Day). Mentor + political guru: G.K. GOKHALE (advised him to spend 1 year travelling India to understand it before politicising). FIRST SATYAGRAHAS in India: (1) CHAMPARAN (Bihar, 1917) — exploitation of indigo planters by British; (2) KHEDA (Gujarat, 1918) — peasants' tax relief during drought; (3) AHMEDABAD MILL strike (1918, textile workers vs owners). Founded SABARMATI ASHRAM (1915, near Ahmedabad) → became HQ of his movements. 1920: launched NON-COOPERATION movement (after Jallianwala Bagh + Khilafat). 1930: SALT MARCH / DANDI (12 March-6 April; 24 days, 240 miles). Followers in S Africa: PRANJEEVAN MEHTA (banker), HENRY POLAK, HERMANN KALLENBACH. Returned by SS ARABIA via London.

questions.stem: Gandhi's POLITICAL MENTOR (in early phase of return to India) was:

options.option_text: Gopal Krishna Gokhale (Servants of India Society)
Lala Lajpat Rai (Punjab Kesari) too alone

questions.explanation: GOPAL KRISHNA GOKHALE (1866-1915) — moderate INC leader; founder of SERVANTS OF INDIA SOCIETY (1905, Poona — trained workers for selfless public service). Gandhi called him 'POLITICAL GURU'. Gokhale visited Gandhi in S Africa (1912); supported his struggle. After Gandhi returned 1915, Gokhale died within months (Feb 1915). Tilak was Gandhi's political GUIDE in another phase ('LOKAMANYA' — beloved of people). MAHATMA title given by RABINDRANATH TAGORE (1915). 'BAPU' (father) — affectionate name. SARDAR PATEL, NEHRU = key followers. Disciples: VINOBA BHAVE (Bhoodan movement, declared Gandhi's spiritual heir), JP NARAYAN. 'GANDHIANS': simplicity, ahimsa, truth, swadeshi, sarvodaya (welfare of all), trusteeship.

questions.explanation: 'MY EXPERIMENTS WITH TRUTH' (1925-29; serialised in his journal NAVAJIVAN). Originally written in GUJARATI ('Satyana Prayogo athwa Atmakatha'); translated to English by his secretary Mahadev Desai. Covers his life from birth to ~1921 (didn't continue to later years). FRANK + SELF-CRITICAL — discusses his shyness, brief meat-eating phase as boy, sexual desires, struggles. 'EXPERIMENTS' reflects his views: every choice = an experiment in truthful living. OTHER GANDHI WRITINGS: 'HIND SWARAJ / Indian Home Rule' (1909, written aboard SS Kildonan Castle from London → S Africa, in 10 days; manifesto on swaraj, modern civilisation critique); 'INDIA OF MY DREAMS' (collected speeches/writings); contributions to YOUNG INDIA + HARIJAN journals; voluminous correspondence. CHIEF source for studying his thought.

questions.stem: Gandhi's FIRST satyagraha in INDIA was at:
questions.explanation: CHAMPARAN SATYAGRAHA (1917) — Bihar. Gandhi's FIRST in India. INDIGO PLANTERS forced peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 (TINKATHIA) of land + sell at fixed low prices to British. RAJ KUMAR SHUKLA — Champaran peasant who travelled to convince Gandhi to come (took several requests). Gandhi went, surveyed, refused court order to leave (DEFIED). British Govt, fearing escalation, set up commission with Gandhi as member; passed CHAMPARAN AGRARIAN ACT (1918) — abolished tinkathia. Major MILESTONE: first defiance of British in India. KEY ASSOCIATES: BRAJ KISHORE PRASAD, RAJENDRA PRASAD (later 1st President of India — 1st time political work; also active in Champaran), JB Kripalani, Mahadev Desai. SAME YEAR (1917): Russian Revolution, world chaos — context.

questions.stem: Gandhi was assassinated on 30 JANUARY 1948 by:

options.option_text: A British agent in disguise (option here)

questions.explanation: 30 JAN 1948, 5:17 PM at BIRLA HOUSE (now GANDHI SMRITI), Delhi. Gandhi shot 3 times in chest at point-blank range during evening prayer meeting on his way to the lawn. Reportedly said 'HE RAM' as he fell (debated by historians). NATHURAM GODSE — Maharashtrian Brahmin, journalist, Hindu Mahasabha activist; with co-conspirator NARAYAN APTE. Reasons: blamed Gandhi for partition + appeasement of Muslims (esp. asking govt to release ₹55 crore to Pakistan). Earlier failed assassination on 20 JAN 1948 by bombing. GODSE + APTE — tried, hanged 15 NOV 1949 at AMBALA Jail. Funeral procession ~1 million people; Nehru's emotional radio address ('LIGHT HAS GONE OUT OF OUR LIVES'). RAJ GHAT (Delhi) = his memorial; cremation site. POSTHUMOUSLY nominated 5× for Nobel Peace Prize but never awarded — 'great omission' acknowledged by Nobel Committee.
